html:
SMTO-CMP-0031 — The AI claimed it made a change, but only an answer is proven

GUID: 1ef6680c-8683-4a49-94d1-8a6d95be447f
Slug: completion-success-status-mismatch
Domain: CMP · Subsystem: cmp

What happened

  • The AI marked the task as an action it completed, but its proof only supports an answer or report. SMTO asked it to label the result as an answer instead. No work needs to be redone.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the task still shows Running, wait. SMTO has told the AI to finish with the answer label, using the same results. Only the label is wrong; the steps and their results stay as they are.
  2. If you asked SMTO to change something, check that thing yourself, or expand the task to see whether a step made the change. Do not rerun the task just to fix the label. The proof showed an answer, not a change, so the change may not have happened.
  3. If the change is missing, send a message asking SMTO to make it and show a check afterward. If it's there, no action is needed. This gets the missing change done without repeating anything that already worked.

What success looks like

  • The task shows Completed with the AI's answer, and anything you asked to change is confirmed in place.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before asking for it again. Open Technical details, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't rerun the task just to fix the label; that could repeat changes.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A completed declaration was rejected, and status-only recovery proved that the same message, evidence and checks validate as answered (suggested_status=answered, original_reason retained).

What this means

  • Status-only recovery proves the same message/evidence/checks validate as answered after a completed declaration was rejected. Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.

Why this can happen

  • Status-only recovery proves the same message/evidence/checks validate as answered after a completed declaration was rejected.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect suggested_status and original_reason; this correction neither chooses new evidence nor independently accepts the task.

How to fix it

  • Inspect suggested_status and original_reason in completion_feedback. Resubmit finish_task with status answered and the unchanged evidence; this correction neither selects new evidence nor accepts the task by itself. Do not rerun work to repair the label. If an action really was required, address original_reason (for example missing mutation evidence).
  • Correct the declaration to the suggested answered status when it accurately represents the task; do not rerun work to repair the label.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The model supplies the supported status and ordinary completion validation accepts the unchanged evidence.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
